productionMetadata.method: Existing read-only catalog exports; no business rows or RPC execution.
productionMetadata.validation: All three final files parsed successfully. No minute-accurate query timestamp established.

prerequisites.consequence: SQL-language sources() references missing relations. Under normal check_function_bodies behavior CREATE FUNCTION fails; the draft cannot simply add four RPCs to this catalog.

actor.observed: auth.uid must equal p_actor; profile id equals p_actor; profile tenant equals requested tenant; user_roles role allowlist business_admin/business_manager/billing/dispatch; public.has_permission chooses edit for write versus view_sensitive for read.
limitations: Assumes profiles.id equals auth user ID; no production identity-row reads establish that equality.
No explicit profile status/is_active or current auth-session expiry check inside this actor helper; has_permission behavior is a separate dependency.
Role allowlist and canonical profile identity require reconciliation with the actual current permission contract.

rlsAndGrants.observed: Private roots/events enable RLS, have no client table grants, and append-only triggers; public wrappers are SECURITY INVOKER. Private schema USAGE is revoked from authenticated, and no subsequent USAGE/private entrypoint EXECUTE grants appear.
rlsAndGrants.effect: The INVOKER wrappers cannot call the private entrypoints as authenticated even after relation prerequisites are solved.
rlsAndGrants.important: Adding schema USAGE alone is not an adequate correction: newly created helper functions also require explicit least-privilege EXECUTE ACL review.

idempotencyAndReceipts.observed: Tenant/employee advisory lock and locked root serialize head update; request_id unique per tenant; exact command comparison and confirm read endpoint exist.
idempotencyAndReceipts.defect: commit_event compares root.head_id against expected before it reads an existing request_id. An identical post-success commit replay uses the old expected head and raises 40001 before its receipt can be returned.
idempotencyAndReceipts.readback: Repository validates exact request/command/event/previous head; uncertain workflow uses a separate confirm-only path. This recovery path does not prove idempotent commit replay.
unverified: No two-session CAS/rollback/deadlock execution for this draft.
No test executed against this draft's actual SQL or public wrappers.

validation.observed: SQL checks some scope/version/kind fields and shallow snapshot originals plus offboard access count.
validation.blocker: It does not enforce the TypeScript payload schema, required field types/date/enum rules, active-person snapshots or full domain transitions. Client validation cannot secure an authenticated raw RPC call.
validation.additionalSourceGap: commit_event does not itself require employee_original(t,e) to exist before creating the root/event; read_context has an employee check, but it is not a substitute for a mutation-side check.
validation.readbackImpact: Strict history/context decoders can reject a server-persisted malformed command, making a ledger unusable through the intended receiver.

contracts.dataMutationBoundary: Prepared operations append evidence roots/events; they are not proof that original employee, payroll, access-provider or HR records changed.

prerequisites.consequence: sources() directly references client_service_records, absent from the final relation catalog. Existing service_records is not proof of a compatible substitution; it needs its own contract review.
prerequisites.existingGrantBoundary: Several present financing source tables have RLS enabled, zero policies and no authenticated CRUD in the final catalog. New SECURITY DEFINER source reads would therefore introduce a controlled read API; existing table RLS alone does not establish its authorization.

actor.observed: Checks auth UID, canonical profile ID and current tenant with null-safe comparisons; JWT exp and auth.sessions/session_id; active bound profile; live role/permission-set checks and exact permissions. Write locks permission/source tables.
limitations: Assumes auth.uid equals actor/profile ID and resolve_current_profile_id equals the same ID; support for distinct profile/auth IDs is not established by metadata.
auth.sessions structure, function-owner privileges, default function ACLs and configured exposed schemas are not covered by the public name-only catalogs.

rlsAndGrants.observed: Private roots/events enable RLS and table grants are revoked; schema USAGE plus read_context/commit_event/confirm_event EXECUTE are granted to authenticated. Other newly created helper functions are not explicitly revoked from PUBLIC.
rlsAndGrants.blocker: Under normal PostgreSQL defaults, helpers such as SECURITY DEFINER sources(t,c) and history(t,c) retain PUBLIC EXECUTE. These helpers take caller-supplied tenant/client IDs and do not call actor(). Schema USAGE makes the SQL privilege boundary wider than the three intended entrypoints.
limits: The patch has not been applied.
No claim of a directly reachable REST exploit: exposure of the private schema and actual default ACLs were not queried.
A private schema/SECURITY DEFINER label does not replace explicit per-function privilege control.

idempotencyAndReceipts.observed: Locks current client and source/role tables, locks root, then looks up prior request before fresh source/CAS validation; exact command comparison returns a prior receipt. Confirm also checks current actor/event owner. Source walk, history-chain validation and correction-target check exist.
idempotencyAndReceipts.positive: Ordering supports identical known-request replay after the head has advanced, unlike the personnel draft.
unverified: No actual SQL execution, SDK/PostgREST wrapper test, role-switching grants test or two-session CAS/deadlock/rollback proof for this draft.

validation.observed: SQL enforces kind-specific payload key sets, nonempty values when a value happens to be a string, and exact source snapshots only for objects carrying kind/id/snapshot.
validation.blocker: Required source values may be null and required numeric/date/enum fields may have inappropriate types. walk_sources(null/number) does nothing. The SQL does not enforce its TypeScript domain contract.
validation.counterexampleLimits: A full command still needs valid current actor/tenant/client IDs, request/event IDs, timestamp/note and expected head. This is a source control-flow counterexample, not an executed write.
validation.readbackImpact: The intended TypeScript validator rejects these values. A malformed persisted event can then make strict history/context loading fail.

contracts.dataMutationBoundary: Prepared operations append evidence ledger records; they do not change native financing, billing, service or proof originals.

findings.summary: Seven public RPCs and seven draft-required relation names across the two packages are absent. Missing relation prerequisites prevent treating these as ready RPC-only additions.
Authenticated public INVOKER wrappers cannot enter the private schema because required privileges are explicitly revoked and not restored.
Private helper execute ACLs are not explicitly restricted; schema USAGE plus default PUBLIC EXECUTE can expose unguarded definer helpers at the SQL boundary. Actual exposed API/default ACLs unknown.
CAS precedes request replay lookup, so successful identical commit retry cannot reach its stored receipt.
Server validators do not enforce the payload/domain contracts required by client decoders; malformed authorized raw requests can create unreadable ledger history.

conclusion.nextReviewableDelta: A new narrowly scoped design must first reconcile actual relation/identity contracts, explicit helper/entrypoint privileges, mutation-side ownership, server domain validation and request/CAS order. Then separate synthetic PostgreSQL/public-wrapper/SDK and concurrency proofs are required.
conclusion.authorization: This report authorizes no application, deployment, migration editing or remote writes.
